claims.claim: The world generated an estimated 62 million tonnes of e-waste in 2022, and only 22.3% was documented as formally collected and recycled.
claims.episode_span: Every year the world discards millions of tons of electronics whose copper, gold, and other metals sit already concentrated above ground.
claims.supporting_quote: In 2022, an estimated 62 million tonnes of e-waste were produced globally. Only 22.3% was documented as formally collected and recycled

claims.claim: A ton of discarded phones/circuit boards contains far more gold than a ton of gold ore - about 100 times more, per the World Economic Forum.
claims.episode_span: A single metric ton of mixed printed circuit boards can hold recoverable metal values that exceed those in many conventional ores by factors of ten or more
claims.source_title: NRRI looks into urban mining - Natural Resources Research Institute, University of Minnesota
claims.supporting_quote: There’s about 100 times more gold in a ton of mobile phones than in a ton of gold ore, according to the World Economic Forum.

claims.claim: Run-of-mine copper ore is low-grade: the average grade of copper ores in the 21st century is below 0.6% copper.
claims.episode_span: the first arrives as run-of-mine copper ore containing perhaps one percent metal by weight
claims.supporting_quote: The average grade of copper ores in the 21st century is below 0.6% copper, with a proportion of economic ore minerals being less than 2% of the total volume of the ore rock.

claims.claim: Standard circuit-board laminates (FR-4) employ bromine-based flame retardants, a contamination concern for recycling.
claims.episode_span: The hard constraints remain contamination from legacy brominated flame retardants, the capital intensity of building new separation capacity
claims.supporting_quote: FR-4 epoxy resin systems typically employ bromine , a halogen, to facilitate flame-resistant properties in FR-4 glass epoxy laminates.
